title: Career Portfolio Playbook and Internal Tools Guide
author: Maya R. Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the Career Portfolio concept at Redwood and provides a practical toolkit for new and returning employees to use internal systems during ramp, development cycles, and role transitions. It merges role ladders, micro-credentialing, benefit touchpoints, and the operational how-to for People Ops and engineering managers. The goal is to reduce friction for career movement and to make tooling predictable and audit-friendly.

Who this is for

- ICs and managers across Engineering, Product, and GTM who are planning rotations, promotions, or lateral moves.
- People Ops partners and Talent Managers who enable role changes and benefits.
- New hires using the onboarding toolchain and managers running onboarding sequences.

Key principles

1. Portfolio-first growth: employees assemble a portfolio (projects + credentials + impact metrics) that maps directly to role expectations.
2. Tool-enabled transparency: all progress must be visible to employees and approvers through People Portal and the Career Dashboard.
3. Safe mobility: we favor predictable lateral moves and short-term rotations to accelerate capability building while preserving team delivery.

Sections

1) Career Portfolio: definition and components

A Career Portfolio is a lightweight collection of:

- Role profile (title, level, core responsibilities)
- 3–6 recent impact examples (metric + context + outcome)
- Supporting artifacts (PRs, design docs, customer feedback)
- Micro-credentials / badges (internal courses, workshops, external certs)

How to structure an entry (recommended template)

1. Title: "Project/Responsibility — YYYY"
2. Context: 1–2 sentences describing scope and constraints
3. Impact metric(s): numeric where possible (e.g., reduced p99 latency by 18% for checkout flow)
4. Role & collaborators: named teammates and owners
5. Artifact links: Confluence, GitHub, Dashboard traces

2) Role ladders, competencies, and micro-badging

- Competency maps live in the Competency Library (People Portal > Career > Competencies). Each role ladder (IC, Manager, Tech Lead) has:
  - Core skills (communication, system design, coding standards)
  - Level behaviors (example: L3 demonstrates autonomous delivery of features end-to-end)
- Micro-badging: short, evidence-based courses (2–8 hours) with automatic badge issuance on completion. Badges feed into Career Dashboard scoring. Current badges: "Production Observability", "Quantization Basics", "Customer Oncall Readiness".

3) Promotion and rotation workflows (manager & employee responsibilities)

Manager checklist for promotion/rotation:

1. Discuss intent with the employee and document a 30/60/90 plan in Confluence.
2. Confirm role requirements and identify missing portfolio artifacts.
3. Open a Mobility Request in People Portal (select "promotion" or "rotation").
4. People Ops schedules calibration panel within 10 business days for promotions; rotations are routed to team leads for approval within 5 business days.

Employee checklist for promotion/rotation:

1. Compile/update Career Portfolio entries; highlight 3 artifacts that demonstrate level expectations.
2. Complete required micro-badges if applicable.
3. Request manager review and submit People Portal Mobility Request.
4. Attend calibration / panel and respond to follow-ups within 3 business days.

SLOs for the mobility process:

- People Ops will acknowledge Mobility Requests within 2 business days.
- Promotions complete calibration and final notification within 21 calendar days in 90% of cases.
- Rotations complete manager approvals and access changes within 10 calendar days in 95% of cases.

4) Benefits alignment and timing during transitions

- Health & leave: benefits enrollment changes triggered by role change will be queued and processed by Benefits Team. Expect processing time of up to one pay cycle.
- Compensation adjustments: promotions with salary changes are applied on the next payroll run following final approval unless otherwise noted.
- Sabbatical & parental leave eligibility: tenure calculations reset only for lateral transfers if there is no employment gap.

5) Internal tools playbook (step-by-step)

Core systems referenced in this playbook: People Portal (internal HRW UI), Onboarder CLI, BadgeMint (micro-badge issuer), Career Dashboard (Confluence + embedded widgets), Access Manager (Okta-provisioning bridge), and FleetPass (badge & office access).

A. Setting up your Career Portfolio (first week)

1. People Portal > Career > Create Portfolio. Use the "starter template" to add 3 artifact links.
2. Run: onboarder init --portfolio --auto from your workstation to pre-fill repo/confluence links.
3. Request contributor access for artifacts: Access Manager ticket RB-req-PORTFOLIO (tag with team and project code).

B. Requesting a Mobility change (promotion/rotation)

1. Manager initiates: People Portal > Mobility > New Request. Fill expected start date, role, and attach portfolio.
2. Employee verifies artifact access and confirms calendar availability for calibration.

C. Badge issuance flow (example: Production Observability)

- Complete the Observability micro-course in Learning Hub.
- Run BadgeMint claim --badge observability --email your-corp-email. Badge appears in Career Dashboard within 4 hours.

D. Access changes on rotation (example steps for engineers)

1. Submit Access Manager change with new-team tag. Example ticket body: "Change owner: alice@redwood.com; new team: serving-runtime; repos: runtime-core, perf-tests; iam role: repo-write".
2. SSO and Okta changes propagate in 2–6 hours; FleetPass physical access changes processed within 24–48 hours for office locations.

6) Manager playbook: onboarding and 90-day ramp

Managers should pair the onboarding plan with the employee's Career Portfolio. Key checkpoints: 1: Week 1 (access & orientation), 2: Week 2 (first project kickoff), 3: Day 30 (initial impact demo), 4: Day 60 (feedback checkpoint), 5: Day 90 (portfolio review and role confirmation).

90-day checklist (copy/paste):

- [ ] Portfolio created and shared
- [ ] Required badges started (at least 1 completed)
- [ ] Mentorship pairing assigned
- [ ] First quantifiable impact recorded
- [ ] Access & billing tags assigned for project resources

7) Audit, compliance, and retention

- People Ops retains Mobility requests, portfolio snapshots, and calibration outcomes for 7 years to support audits and compensation reviews.
- Access Manager audit logs are connected to the Security SIEM and reviewed monthly for unexpected access spikes.

Table: common request types and SLA expectations

| Request type | Typical owner | SLA (target) | Notes |
|--------------|---------------|-------------|-------|
| New hire portfolio creation | Employee/Manager | 2 business days | Template in People Portal |
| Mobility (rotation) | Manager | 5 business days to approve | People Ops notification auto-sent |
| Mobility (promotion) | People Ops / Calibration Panel | 21 calendar days | Escalate to Head of People if delayed > 30 days |
| Access provisioning | Access Manager | 24–48 hours | Depends on external vendor windows |

8) Frequently asked questions

Q: Can I apply for a promotion without a manager recommendation?
A: Yes. Self-nominations are supported. The Mobility Request must include manager acknowledgment (they will receive an auto-notification and must respond within 3 business days).

Q: How are external certifications weighted?
A: External certs count as supporting evidence. Core decisions are driven by the portfolio artifacts and demonstrated behaviors on the competency map.

Q: What if my badge does not appear?
A: File a BadgeMint ticket with the claim ID and your corp email. Resolutions typically within 3 business days.

9) Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: People Ops (policy and process).
- Tooling and automation owner: Eng Dev Tools team (Onboarder CLI, BadgeMint).
- Escalation path: People Ops -> Head of People -> Chief People Officer. For access incidents: Security -> CISO.

Related resources (quick links)

Appendix A: Example portfolio entry (copyable)

Title: "KV-cache prefix optimization — Q3 2025"
Context: Reduced unnecessary cache lookups by pruning prefix matching in the runtime router for high-cardinality prompts.
Impact: p99 end-to-end generation latency improved from 1.32s to 1.08s for 512-token requests (18% improvement), cost per 1k tokens decreased by 9%.
Role & collaborators: Owner: mchen@redwood.com; collaborators: runtime-team, perf-eng
Artifacts: https://confluence.redwood/internal/kv-pruning-design, https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4821

Appendix B: CLI snippets

- Initialize portfolio (local):
  onboarder init --portfolio --name "KV-cache prefix optimization" --link https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4821
- Claim badge:
  badgemint claim --badge production-observability --email mchen@redwood.com
